Internal note
“Dex” and “Dexter” are welcome informal nicknames. Formal product naming remains ChannelDex.

Capital Media Systems · Identity Standard 001

Institutional permanence. Modern usability.

ChannelDex is a television programming management application for multi-channel public-media environments. Its identity is established, technical, organized, and durable, historically informed and never artificially aged.

Version 1.2DraftSeptember 2026
01

Foundation

Name, architecture, character

ChannelDex is the product. Capital Media Systems is the developer, publisher, and parent identity. Their relationship is close, but their roles remain clear.

Brand architecture

PRIMARY PRODUCT

ChannelDex

The formal product name is always ChannelDex. In formal introductions, the preferred relationship is ChannelDex by Capital Media Systems, with ChannelDex visually dominant.

PARENT IDENTITY

Capital Media Systems

The developer, publisher, and owner behind ChannelDex. It may appear independently on corporate documentation, software publishing material, title pages, About screens, and future products.

Naming standard

UseFormGuidance
FormalChannelDexDocumentation, interfaces, packaging, and public communication.
Contextual uppercaseCHANNELDEXPermitted only where all-uppercase typography belongs to the surrounding layout.
Informal / internalDex or DexterFriendly shorthand, never a substitute for the formal product name.
Do not useChannel Dex · ChannelDEXIncorrect word division or capitalization.

Product descriptor

TELEVISION PROGRAMMING MANAGEMENT

The descriptor explains the product category but is not part of the ChannelDex name. Omit it when context already establishes the product’s purpose.

Brand character

COMPETENTORGANIZEDTECHNICALINSTITUTIONALQUIETLY DISTINCTIVESLIGHTLY DRYDURABLECONFIDENT
Not the brief: cute, cartoonish, consumer-oriented, cyberpunk, SaaS-generic, government clip-art-like, or nostalgic for nostalgia’s sake.
02

Identity system

Choose the simplest complete mark

The supplied master artwork is authoritative. Never recreate the wordmark, endorsement, rule, descriptor, or corporate mark with ordinary typography.

Primary product lockup

ChannelDex Full Logo ColorMaster supplied

Preferred for login screens, title pages, documentation covers, websites, presentations, promotional material, packaging, and installations with sufficient horizontal space.

Extended lockup

ChannelDex Full Logo Color with TaglineMaster supplied

Use for introductory applications where the function of ChannelDex should be immediately clear. The descriptor is part of this approved artwork and should not be manually attached to another lockup.

Product-only lockup

ChannelDex Only ColorMaster supplied
ChannelDex Only GrayscaleMaster supplied

Use after ChannelDex has already been identified, where space is restricted, or where the corporate endorsement would reproduce too small.

Grayscale configurations

Primary grayscaleMaster supplied
Extended grayscaleMaster supplied

Use grayscale where color is unavailable, the surrounding design needs reduced visual competition, or printing requires tonal neutrality. Grayscale artwork is not a substitute for a true one-color master.

Approved grayscale record values: Station Blue becomes #2A2A2A, Monitor Green becomes #444444, and Broadcast Red becomes #6D6D6D.

Reverse master

Full Logo InvertedMaster supplied

Use the approved reverse master on Charcoal or other validated dark fields. Do not simulate a reverse logo by applying filters or converting a grayscale export.

03

Symbol & spacing

Three records. Many meanings.

The framed records suggest program entries, schedule slots, media records, index cards, channel positions, and a display, without fixing a single canonical interpretation.

The ChannelDex symbol

The symbol is a heavy rounded rectangular frame containing three horizontal information records. The three records do not represent exactly three television channels or exactly 3 corporate concepts.

Fixed record order:
STATION BLUE
MONITOR GREEN
BROADCAST RED

Clear space

Define X as the vertical height of one colored record. Maintain at least 1X around the standalone symbol and app icon, and 1.5X around complete lockups. More space is preferred.

Clear space contains no text, borders, controls, photographs, competing marks, or decorative elements. The official horizontal rule is part of the artwork and is exempt.

Minimum reproduction size

AssetRecommended digital minimum
Favicon16 px
Standalone ChannelDex symbol24 px high
ChannelDex-only lockup140 px wide
Full ChannelDex / CMS lockup220 px wide
Extended descriptor lockup300 px wide
Capital Media Systems corporate mark220 px wide

These are initial production standards. Validate them against final vector masters before fixing them permanently.

Application icon and favicon

Application iconMaster supplied

Use for launchers, installation packages, catalogs, desktop applications, and operating-system surfaces. Do not reconstruct it inside an arbitrary rounded rectangle.

Compact markMaster supplied

Use for browser favicons, bookmarks, compact browser UI, and markers where the complete icon loses clarity.

04

Color system

Structure first. Signal second.

These canonical sRGB values supersede colors sampled from earlier raster exports. Print conversions should be established from controlled proofs.

CHARCOAL#181A1B
STATION BLUE#234C74
MONITOR GREEN#475F43
BROADCAST RED#7D2828
WARM PAPER#F4E4CC
CAPITAL BLUE#00529B

Color roles

CHARCOALPrimary wordmark, symbol frame, typography, rules, and dark structure. Prefer it to pure black.
STATION BLUEPrincipal ChannelDex accent, upper record, selected navigation, information graphics, and technical rules.
MONITOR GREENSecond record and secondary brand accent. It is not automatically the color for every successful state.
BROADCAST REDLower record, “Dex” emphasis, and high-emphasis brand applications. It is not inherently an error color.
WARM PAPERDocumentation, icon backgrounds, packaging, presentation fields, and branded introductory surfaces.
CAPITAL BLUECapital Media Systems dome, corporate rules, and parent-brand applications. Never substitute it for Station Blue.

Accessibility against Warm Paper Beige

CHARCOAL14.0:1
STATION BLUE7.1:1
MONITOR GREEN5.6:1
BROADCAST RED7.6:1
CAPITAL BLUE6.3:1
Dark-surface caution: the colored brand tones do not provide sufficient contrast against Charcoal for ordinary small text. Use white, Warm Paper Beige, or another validated light foreground. Color must never carry status by itself.

Background use

Preferred fields are Warm Paper Beige, white, and Charcoal with an appropriate reversed master. Avoid complex photography, noisy textures, arbitrary gradients, and colors that obscure the three records.

05

Typography

Computing heritage, without theater

The wordmarks are custom artwork. IBM Plex is the accepted supporting family for interfaces, manuals, presentations, and technical communications.

Program information,
made legible.

IBM Plex Sans carries headings, body copy, navigation, captions, and labels. Its corporate grotesk structure and computing heritage support the identity without performing “retro.”

CITY-TV / 2026-09-11 / 19:00
CDX-PRG-00417 / MEDIA READY

IBM Plex Mono is reserved for identifiers, timestamps, filenames, version numbers, database values, and terminal-oriented material.

Accepted: IBM Plex is the supporting type family for ChannelDex interfaces, manuals, presentations, and technical communications.

06

Graphic language

Information becomes the ornament

Record rows, schedule blocks, database fields, labels, technical rules, and modular panels provide the visual grammar. They remain subordinate to actual information.

RECORD MOTIF

Use sparingly as section markers, dividers, packaging bands, and selected navigation indicators.

SCHEDULE STRUCTURE

07:00Program block07:30Station information08:00Next program

Repeated use on every available surface turns a useful motif into decoration. The brand’s historical character comes from proportion and discipline, not from visual noise.

Period influence

Use as reference

  • Corporate identity manuals
  • Institutional computing
  • Database software and catalog systems
  • Broadcast-equipment manufacturers
  • NAB-era technical literature
  • Equipment labels and software packaging

Do not simulate

  • Yellowed paper or faux distressing
  • CRT bloom, scan lines, or phosphor glow
  • VHS noise or terminal flicker
  • Arcade imagery or pixel fonts
  • Synthwave motifs and neon palettes
  • Fake low-resolution graphics
07

Application

A modern interface with a long memory

ChannelDex should not simulate a 1986 computer. It should inherit the era’s information discipline while remaining responsive, accessible, familiar, and efficient.

ChannelDexPUB-TV / THURSDAY
TodayScheduleProgramsMediaHistory
TimeProgramMediaStatus
07:00Community JournalEP-0417Prepared
07:30Station informationPSA rotationPlanned
08:00City Council ReplayMEET-0910Scheduled

Illustrative, not a UI specification. Brand colors and functional UI colors serve different purposes. Do not force all three record colors into every control or status.

Digital accessibility

ChannelDex products target WCAG 2.2 AA at minimum: 4.5:1 contrast for normal text, 3:1 for large text, visible focus, understandable states, non-color indicators for workflow conditions, and practical type sizes. Where accessibility and strict color use conflict, accessibility takes precedence.

Capital Media Systems

Capital Media Systems Corporate MarkMaster supplied

The independent corporate mark is based on the Michigan State Capitol dome and uses Capital Blue. Its defining components are the dome, corporate wordmark, interrupted rule, and the approved tagline: PROGRAMMING A BRIGHTER TOMORROW.

Keep it subordinate beside ChannelDex. Do not place the Capitol dome inside the ChannelDex symbol, add ChannelDex records to the corporate mark, replace Station Blue with Capital Blue, or turn the corporate mark into an application icon.

08

Governance

Protect the system by using it consistently

The master artwork controls proportions, color order, wordmark construction, endorsement placement, horizontal rules, and descriptor relationships.

Incorrect logo use

  • Do not stretch, compress, rotate, mirror, or skew.
  • Do not alter symbol proportions or reorder records.
  • Do not recolor records or substitute Capital Blue.
  • Do not recreate either wordmark with typed text.
  • Do not reposition the endorsement or alter the rule.
  • Do not add shadows, bevels, glows, outlines, or effects.
  • Do not place the Capitol dome inside ChannelDex.
  • Do not use Dex or Dexter as the public name.
  • Do not attach the descriptor to an unapproved lockup.
  • Do not use a screenshot when master artwork exists.

Versioning

Version 1.2, Draft is the current working baseline. This minor increment records the accepted supporting typeface decision and clarified symbol language. The remaining open work is limited to the true one-color masters.

Change typeVersion action
Editorial corrections or layout refinements that do not change a standardRecord in the change log without necessarily changing the version.
New or clarified standards that affect production, such as approved grayscale values or an additional master variantIncrement the minor version, for example 1.3 Draft.
Formal approval after open assets and provisional decisions are resolvedPromote the current minor version from Draft to Accepted.
Changes to logo construction, color roles, brand hierarchy, or other system foundationsStart a new major version, for example 2.0 Draft.
